title: Worksheet 12: Tuples (V2.0)
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: A tuple is a data structure similar to a list, since it also stores multiple values together in a specific order, but with one major difference: once a tuple is created, its contents generally cannot be changed, added to, or removed, a property known as being "immutable." This is different from a list, which is "mutable," meaning a list's contents can be freely changed after it is created. Because a tuple's values cannot be accidentally modified later in a program, tuples are often used to store information that should always stay the same throughout a program, such as a fixed set of coordinates, the exact number of days in each month, or a set of unchanging configuration settings. Like both strings and lists, tuples support indexing, meaning individual values inside a tuple can still be accessed directly using their position, even though those values cannot be altered afterward. Choosing between a list and a tuple often comes down to a simple question: does this collection of values need to be changed later, or should it always stay exactly the same?

questions.text: According to the paragraph, what does it mean that a tuple is "immutable"?
questions.correct: Its contents generally cannot be changed after it is created
distractors: It can grow to any size

questions.text: According to the paragraph, a list is described as:
questions.correct: Mutable, meaning its contents can be freely changed

questions.text: According to the paragraph, can individual values inside a tuple be accessed by position?
distractors: No, tuples have no order at all
Only after the tuple is converted into a list
Only if the tuple holds exactly two values

questions.text: A program stores the number of days in each month, which never changes. Based on the paragraph, which structure fits best?
questions.correct: A tuple, because the values should always stay the same
distractors: A list, because the values will need to be updated often
A boolean, because there are only two options
A string, because the values are labels

questions.text: Based on the paragraph, what is the main advantage of a tuple over a list for fixed data?
questions.correct: The values cannot be accidentally modified later in the program
distractors: The values can be sorted more quickly
The values take up no memory at all
The values can be accessed without any index
